title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer closer to OpenAI's tool calling semantics so downstream SDKs (Python/TS) and the hosted API behave consistently when models return tool_choice, when multiple tools map to the same schema, and when tools emit preformatted messages. Changes: 1) Add schema mapping to tool registry so tools can declare a canonical JSON Schema -> Redwood will use schema ids to dedupe and map incoming tool arguments to the right tool implementation. 2) Implement tool_choice semantics: preserve original tool message payload (including role/name) and attach a normalized 'tool_choice' object to the response to match OpenAI behavior. 3) Tool message formatting: ensure messages created by tools are accepted as-is when the model indicates a 'tool_choice' and also provide an opt-in normalization layer for SDKs. Compatibility: added extensive integration tests exercising edge cases (multi-tool match, partial-schema match, tool message with embedded function call syntax). This PR also updates SDKs (python + ts examples) and docs. Checklist: - [x] schema mapping implementation - [x] tool_choice semantics + backward-compatible API surface - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] SDK example updates - [x] docs updated (openai-compat/tool-calling.md) Related: Linear ENG-1283, ENG-1398. Linked incident: SUP-3421 (customer reported mismatch in tool_choice payloads).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall looks good. Two questions: 1) when two tools map to the same schema_id, which tool gets priority at runtime? 2) Can you add a small migration note for customers who rely on previous canonicalization?

Priya Nair: Response: priority is deterministic based on registered tool priority + lexical name as tiebreaker. Added migration note in docs and an opt-out flag (openaiCompat.toolMessageNormalize=false).
Samir Patel: Tests look thorough. Suggest adding an explicit test where a tool returns malformed JSON but still a valid message string (we should treat as raw message).
Priya Nair: Added test case (integration) to verify malformed JSON in tool message is preserved as raw message and surfaced in logs; does not crash the response pipeline.
Lena Fischer: Small perf question: do we copy the entire tool message payload on every request? This could increase memory usage for large tool responses.
Priya Nair: We attach a reference to the original tool message and only deep-copy when normalization is requested. Added comments and a benchmark in perf-canary showing <2% overhead in typical cases.
release_notes: openai-compat: Add schema_id-based tool registry mapping, implement OpenAI-compatible tool_choice semantics, and introduce opt-in tool message normalization. SDK examples updated. No breaking changes by default; opt-in normalization behind feature flag.
